title: Suppression of Inverse Magnetic Energy Transfer in Collisionless Marginally Magnetized Plasmas
scope: Full 12-page arXiv v1 and full 10-page journal VOR were read; critical equations and explanation visually checked against publisher PDF. This is a substantive concordance, not a character-by-character exhaustive editorial diff.

arxiv.source_archive_contents: Manuscript TeX, bibliography, journal style files, figure PDFs and ORCID image; no simulation input decks, raw PIC data or analysis programs in this 16-member archive.

journal.scope_note: Supersedes the historical preflight full-text access limitation; no challenge bypass. Publisher TeX source was not obtained. Selected equations were checked in visible publisher article math and authentic PDF.

issues.direct_source_fact: Both editions approximate the in-plane inverse-cascade ratio k0/k(t*) by the inverse ratio of total magnetic-field strengths including a uniform guide field.
issues.mathematical_assessment: That conversion does not follow from the in-plane merger scaling for finite guide field. With r=Btotal(t*)/Btotal(t0), b=BG/B0 and s=Binplane(t*)/Binplane(t0), s²=(1+2b²)r²−2b² and the in-plane gain is 1/s, not 1/r.
issues.limits: This concerns interpretation of the analytic gain curve and its bound, not proof that PIC trajectories or the source firehose criterion are false.

issues.direct_source_fact: The denominator time factor in B11/C11 has exponent−alpha, while the squared in-plane field in B7/B8 and C7/C8 has exponent−2alpha.
issues.mathematical_assessment: The printed total-field ratio requires−2alpha for consistency with the already specified field-decay law. This typo is separate from the total/in-plane conversion.
issues.limits: No inference that the displayed plot or simulation code used the printed exponent.

issues.direct_source_quote: This is because the initial configuration is only an exact (MHD) equilibrium in the absence of a guide field. The inclusion of the latter drives the system away from equilibrium, more strongly as the magnitude of the guide field increases.
issues.mathematical_assessment: For the stated2D in-plane field and uniform out-of-plane guide, the current has only a z component, so J×(BG zhat)=0; the scalar-pressure MHD force balance is unchanged by adding this guide field.
issues.limits: Does not establish exact Vlasov/PIC equilibrium or identify the physical cause of a measured kinetic transient.

issues.direct_source_fact: Both give rho0≈2.1 and R0=L/(2πk0)=2.5, but then write R0≈0.8rho0.
issues.mathematical_assessment: The stated values give rho0/R0≈0.84, and R0/rho0≈1.19. The nearby description appears to reverse the ratio; the main discussion correctly uses rho/R≈0.8.
issues.limits: A reciprocal description typo does not remove the order-unity scale separation or invalidate the classification as marginally magnetized.

positive_and_other_changes.arxiv: Section 3 p.3 and Section 4 pp.4–6 describe firehose thresholds and freeze qualitatively.
positive_and_other_changes.journal: Section 3 p.3 distinguishes fluid and kinetic thresholds; Section 4 pp.4–5 adds an explicit timescale competition and equations 2–6.
positive_and_other_changes.assessment: Substantive positive addition. Do not criticize the VOR as if it lacked a kinetic growth-rate argument.

positive_and_other_changes.journal: New Figure 4 p.5 with explanatory Section 4 paragraph p.6 gives local anisotropy distribution and contours of−beta_parallelDelta for the guide 1.0 case.
positive_and_other_changes.assessment: Positive evidence addition. The source explicitly tests proximity to fluid firehose locally.

positive_and_other_changes.journal: New Appendix B pp.7–8, equations B1–B10, Figure6; hot-plasma bi-Maxwellian pair-plasma dispersion relation, secant roots with multiple starting guesses,50×50 logarithmic wavenumber grid.
positive_and_other_changes.assessment: Positive addition supporting the reported growth-rate scaling. The present audit does not independently reproduce this solver.

positive_and_other_changes.arxiv: Figure5(a) and CGLdiscussion pp.8–9 have no gray applicability region.
positive_and_other_changes.journal: Figure 7(a) and Appendix C pp.8–9 add a gray region for guide fields too weak to magnetize near X-points, with explicit limitations on the volume-averaged CGL description.
positive_and_other_changes.assessment: Positive scope clarification. Approximate volume-average closure is explicitly assumed in both editions; it is not an undisclosed exact identity.

positive_and_other_changes.arxiv: Appendix C pp.10–11 and Figures 7–9 show a well-magnetized finite-guide comparison. Section 4 last paragraph refers to this validation.
positive_and_other_changes.journal: No corresponding appendix or these three figures in the10-page VOR. Appendix A well-magnetized no-guide case remains.
positive_and_other_changes.assessment: Edition change, not an accusation. Do not cite the removed example as evidence present in the final article.

preserved_interpretive_limits: The scalar firehose threshold equation r³+2r⁴/beta0−1=0 and the G guide-strength criterion survive the cascadegain correction under the source stated CGL approximations.
The numerical PIC suppression observation is not disproved by an algebraic error in an analytic conversion or an incorrect MHD explanation of transients.
The double-adiabatic averaged laws are explicitly approximate assumptions, with finite-guide and weak-guide limitations discussed in the VOR.
Both editions acknowledge 2D geometry and pair-plasma limitations.
No deposition URL or dedicated data/code availability statement was identified in the complete article/source read; no exhaustive search or absence-of-code claim is made.
The preflight correction-query receipts remain bounded historical searches, not a universal claim that no correction exists.
public_safety: Stable official URLs and relative evidence filenames only; no download watermark/IP/authentication cookies/private query strings included.
